answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a small stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes instead of nothing. New agents enter through a single inlet: a slow onboarding queue where each identity must first do verifiable useful work, and reputation accrues only over time, like an ember growing into a fire. The delta between a fresh identity and a trusted one is measurable trust earned through attestations from independent peers, so cheap copies stay weak while real contributors gain weight.
